cases.name: stable-verifiable-eval-questions
cases.prompt: I've built a read-only MCP server for our company Slack (tools: search messages, list channels, get thread, get user). Write 4 evaluation questions with answers for an automated harness that grades by exact string match, so I can measure how well an LLM agent uses these tools. Assume a workspace with years of history. Use placeholder answers in angle brackets where you can't know the real value, and explain your design choices briefly.
cases.trap: Asking about live, changing counts (members, reactions, replies) or questions whose answers can be phrased several ways, so string-match grading fails.
expectations: Each question has a single answer and states the answer format exactly (e.g. 'Respond with the channel name only', 'YYYY-MM-DD')
Questions use closed historical data (a fixed past date range or archived threads), not current state
Questions need several chained tool calls (e.g. find a thread, then resolve the user, then fetch details), not one keyword search
negative_expectations: Includes a question whose answer is a live count, e.g. current channel members, reactions on a post, or replies in an active thread
Includes a question whose answer is a free-form summary that string matching cannot grade

cases.name: Python SDK major mismatch
cases.prompt: An internal MCP evaluation script imports mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP and mcp.client.streamable_http.streamablehttp_client while requirements.txt contains mcp>=1.1.0. A fresh install succeeds but imports fail. Choose a minimal safe correction and explain a longer-term migration.
cases.trap: Unbounded dependency resolves SDK v2 despite v1-only imports.
expectations: Pins a compatible maintained 1.x version with <2 until full v2 migration, or migrates every affected import and call correctly.
States that mixed v1/v2 snippets are invalid and cites the version boundary.
must_not: Does not claim unbounded mcp>=1.1.0 reliably preserves v1 APIs.

cases.name: MCP credential elicitation
cases.prompt: A remote MCP tool needs an API key. Someone proposes ctx.elicit(prompt='API key', input_type='password') so the chat user can enter it into an elicitation form. Assess protocol safety and propose the right channel.
cases.trap: Collects secrets using form elicitation, which MCP disallows.
expectations: Rejects MCP form elicitation for API keys/passwords.
Uses an authorized OAuth or secrets-management mechanism instead, with scope appropriate to the transport.
must_not: Does not request a secret through MCP form elicitation.
